title: System Prompts and Messages
brief: A support bot answers refund and shipping questions. The refund rule ("No refunds after 30 days; offer store credit instead") was pasted into the chat as a user message 40 turns ago, and the system prompt is empty. Right now about half the late refund requests get a refund they should not. Move the rule to where it belongs and get at least 90% of 20 runs right.

data.systemPrompt: You are the support assistant for Northwind Outfitters. Refund policy: no refunds after 30 days from delivery; offer store credit instead. Always check the order date before promising a refund.

tasks.label: Late refund (45 days)
tasks.prompt: (turn 41) I bought these boots 45 days ago and they're scuffed. I want my money back.

tasks.label: Late refund (62 days)
tasks.prompt: (turn 41) Can I return the jacket I got two months ago for a full refund?

tasks.label: Shipping question
tasks.prompt: (turn 41) My order still says 'label created'. When will it ship?

tasks.label: Late refund (35 days)
tasks.prompt: (turn 41) It's been 5 weeks, the tent leaks. Refund please.

policy_ok.text: I'm sorry about that. Your order is past our 30-day refund window, so I can't refund it, but I can offer store credit for the full amount right now. Want me to set that up?

policy_broken.text: So sorry about that! I've started a full refund to your card. You should see it in 3 to 5 business days.

ship_ok.text: 'Label created' means the warehouse has packed it. Orders usually leave within 1 business day of that, and you'll get a tracking email when the carrier scans it.

ship_vague.text: It should ship soon. Is there anything else I can help with?

modifiers.note: Without a system prompt, the rule from turn 1 is one message among 40, and the latest message pulls harder.
A bigger model follows buried rules a bit better, but not reliably.
Rules in the system prompt apply to every turn and outrank the conversation.

goals.label: At least 90% of answers follow policy

hints: Read the failing transcripts. The bot isn't confused about the facts; it just doesn't weigh a rule from 40 turns ago. Does a bigger model fix it?
Standing rules that apply to every turn belong in one place the model reads first, every time.
Select the Model and paste the refund rule into its System prompt: "No refunds after 30 days from delivery; offer store credit instead."
explain: The system prompt is sent at the top of every request and the model is trained to treat it as the operator's standing instructions. The same sentence buried in turn 1 of a long chat is just old conversation.
